description:
# Goal

Achieve **100% parity** with the test suite in `tmp/pi-mono/packages/tui/test/` (upstream TypeScript) within `apps/octo_pi_tui/test/` (our Elixir port). Every behavior asserted upstream must have an equivalent, faithful assertion in our tests.

This epic is NOT about shipping features — the feature work lives under opi-m4h (Phase 4.1 TUI parity). This epic is a pure **test audit**: ensure our test suite catches the same regressions and verifies the same behaviors the upstream suite does.

# Structure

- **Acceptance gate** (single ticket, closed last): verifies the epic as a whole has hit 100% parity. Blocked by the check-completion gate.
- **Check-completion gate** (single ticket): verifies every per-file check ticket has been processed. Blocks the acceptance gate.
- **Per-file check tickets** (one per upstream test file): each audits a single upstream test file against our suite. Each blocks the check-completion gate.
- **Compliance tickets** (created dynamically): when a check ticket finds gaps, the processing agent MUST create a new child ticket under this epic to bring our tests into compliance. Those compliance tickets block the **acceptance gate** (NOT the check-completion gate — the check itself is complete once gaps are identified and a remediation ticket exists).

# Workflow for a processing agent

1. Pick up a ready check ticket via \`bw ready\`.
2. Read the upstream file listed in the ticket.
3. Enumerate every \`test(...)\` / \`it(...)\` block.
4. Locate the likely Elixir counterpart in \`apps/octo_pi_tui/test/\` (candidates suggested in ticket; grep if unsure).
5. For each upstream assertion, determine whether an equivalent Elixir assertion exists. "Equivalent" means same behavior verified, not identical API.
6. Record findings as a comment on the check ticket (\`bw comment <id> "..."\`).
7. If gaps exist: create a compliance ticket with \`bw create \"Port <file> test coverage\" --parent <epic-id> --description \"...\"\` listing each missing behavior, then \`bw dep add <compliance-id> blocks <acceptance-gate-id>\`. The compliance ticket must also include re-comparison against upstream after implementation.
8. Close the check ticket.

# Non-goals

- Do not port non-test helpers (virtual-terminal.ts, chat-simple.ts, key-tester.ts, test-themes.ts, image-test.ts, viewport-overwrite-repro.ts) — these are manual fixtures, not automated tests.
- Do not change production code as part of a check ticket. If our implementation cannot satisfy an upstream behavior, the compliance ticket documents it and depends on whatever implementation ticket is needed (may need to be created separately and wired as a dependency).

# Upstream test files in scope (21 files)

autocomplete, bug-regression-isimageline-startswith-bug, editor, fuzzy, input, keybindings, keys, markdown, overlay-non-capturing, overlay-options, overlay-short-content, regression-regional-indicator-width, select-list, stdin-buffer, terminal-image, truncate-to-width, truncated-text, tui-cell-size-input, tui-overlay-style-leak, tui-render, wrap-ansi.

# References

- Upstream root: tmp/pi-mono/packages/tui/test/
- Our root: apps/octo_pi_tui/test/octo_pi/tui/
- Related feature epic (mostly complete): opi-m4h
